One-Week Vegetarian Meal Plan

Seven days of balanced, flavorful meals, plus three featured recipes.

Weekly Meal Plan

This plan is lacto-ovo vegetarian and builds in leftovers to save time. Meals marked with ★ have full recipes later in this document.

Recipe 1: Chickpea & Spinach Coconut Curry

Prep: 10 minCook: 25 minServes: 4Diet: Vegan, gluten-free

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive or coconut oil
  • 1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 2 tbsp curry powder
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • ½ tsp turmeric
  • 1 can (14 oz / 400 g) diced tomatoes
  • 1 can (14 oz / 400 ml) full-fat coconut milk
  • 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 5 oz (150 g) fresh baby spinach
  • 1 tbsp lime juice
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • Fresh cilantro and cooked basmati rice, to serve

Instructions

  1. Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or pot over medium heat.
  2. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and translucent.
  3. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
  4. Add the curry powder, cumin and turmeric. Stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
  5. Pour in the diced tomatoes and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 3 minutes.
  6. Add the coconut milk and chickpeas. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
  7. Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, about 2 minutes.
  8. Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
  9. Serve hot over rice, garnished with cilantro.

Nutrition Facts (per serving, curry only, without rice)

NutrientAmount
Calories440 kcal
Total Fat26 g
Saturated Fat16 g
Carbohydrates42 g
Dietary Fiber11 g
Sugars8 g
Protein14 g
Sodium520 mg

Cooking Tips

  • Use full-fat coconut milk for the creamiest texture. Light coconut milk gives a thinner sauce.
  • Add a pinch of chili flakes or a diced fresh chili for more heat.
  • The curry tastes even better the next day and keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days.
  • It freezes well for up to 3 months. Leave out the spinach and add it fresh when reheating.
  • For extra protein, stir in cubes of pan-fried paneer or firm tofu.

Recipe 2: Black Bean & Sweet Potato Tacos

Prep: 15 minCook: 30 minServes: 4 (8 tacos)Diet: Vegan option, dairy-free

Ingredients

Filling

  • 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1 lb / 450 g), peeled and cut into ½-inch cubes
  • 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp chili powder
  • 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) black beans, drained and rinsed
  • Salt, to taste

Lime Crema

  • ½ cup (120 g) Greek yogurt or dairy-free yogurt
  • Juice and zest of 1 lime
  • 1 small clove garlic, grated
  • Pinch of salt

To Serve

  • 8 small corn or flour tortillas
  • 1 ripe avocado, sliced
  • 1 cup shredded red cabbage
  • ¼ cup pickled red onion
  • Fresh cilantro and lime wedges

Instructions

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1½ tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, chili powder and ½ tsp salt.
  3. Spread in a single layer on the baking sheet. Roast for 22–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
  4. While the potatoes roast, warm the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the black beans with a pinch of salt and a splash of water. Cook for 4–5 minutes, lightly mashing a few beans with a fork.
  5. Make the crema by whisking together the yogurt, lime juice, lime zest, garlic and salt. Add a teaspoon of water if it is too thick to drizzle.
  6. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 20–30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.
  7. Assemble each taco with beans, roasted sweet potato, cabbage, avocado and pickled onion. Drizzle with lime crema and top with cilantro.
  8. Serve right away with lime wedges.

Nutrition Facts (per serving, 2 tacos with corn tortillas)

NutrientAmount
Calories490 kcal
Total Fat19 g
Saturated Fat3.5 g
Carbohydrates70 g
Dietary Fiber17 g
Sugars9 g
Protein15 g
Sodium430 mg

Cooking Tips

  • Cut the sweet potatoes into even pieces so they roast at the same rate. Don't crowd the pan, or they will steam instead of crisp.
  • Warming the tortillas makes them pliable and stops them from cracking.
  • Quick pickled onion: soak thin red onion slices in lime juice with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes.
  • Make the filling ahead and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Use leftovers in burrito bowls or salads.
  • Swap the crema for a spoonful of salsa verde to keep the tacos fully vegan.

Recipe 3: Creamy Mushroom & Herb Pasta

Prep: 10 minCook: 20 minServes: 4Diet: Vegetarian

Ingredients

  • 12 oz (340 g) fettuccine or pappardelle
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp butter
  • 1 lb (450 g) cremini mushrooms, sliced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 shallots, finely diced
  • ½ cup (120 ml) dry white wine or vegetable broth
  • 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream
  • ½ cup (50 g) freshly grated Parmesan (use a vegetarian-certified hard cheese if needed), plus extra to serve
  • 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
  • 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
  • 1 tsp lemon juice
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until al dente, following the package directions. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
  2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
  3. Add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for another 4–5 minutes, until deeply golden. Season with salt.
  4. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the shallots, garlic and thyme and cook for 2 minutes until soft and fragrant.
  5. Pour in the wine and simmer for 2–3 minutes, scraping the pan, until mostly evaporated.
  6. Add the cream and simmer gently for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
  7. Add the drained pasta and Parmesan to the skillet. Toss, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats the noodles smoothly.
  8. Remove from the heat. Stir in the parsley and lemon juice, then season with pepper and more salt if needed.
  9. Serve immediately with extra Parmesan.

Nutrition Facts (per serving)

NutrientAmount
Calories650 kcal
Total Fat33 g
Saturated Fat17 g
Carbohydrates67 g
Dietary Fiber4 g
Sugars6 g
Protein20 g
Sodium390 mg

Cooking Tips

  • Don't crowd the mushrooms. Cook them in two batches if your skillet is small, so they brown rather than steam.
  • Salt the mushrooms after they brown, since early salting draws out moisture.
  • Starchy pasta water helps the sauce cling to the noodles. Add it gradually.
  • Traditional Parmesan contains animal rennet. Look for vegetarian-labeled hard cheese if you avoid it.
  • For a lighter version, replace half the cream with whole milk, or use full-fat oat cream for a dairy-free option.
  • Mix mushroom types, such as shiitake or oyster, for deeper flavor.
